text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

American inventor THOMAS EDISON, who took out more than a thousand patents and whose 'firsts' included the electric light bulb, the gramophone and motion pictures, was born on this day in 1847. Today is celebrated as "NATIONAL INVENTOR'S DAY" in the United States.
American film director JOSEPH MANKIEWICZ, who won Oscars for best screenplay and best director on 2 separate occasions for "LETTER TO THREE WIVES" and "ALL ABOUT EVE", was born in 1909.
English fashion designer MARY QUANT was born in 1934.
American film and television star BURT REYNOLDS, was born on this day in 1936.

The truly one-hit-wonder BOBBY 'BORIS' PICKETT was born in 1940. He attempted a career as a film actor and then tried his hand at composing. He wrote "Monster Mash" which was released in time for Halloween in 1962. It went to number one but did not chart in the United Kingdom until 1973. The BBC refused to play it in 1962. When it was released there was renewed interest in BOBBY and it was rumoured he was found driving a taxi in New York.
Brazilian musician SERGIO MENDES was born in 1941. He became internationally known with SERGIO MENDES and Brazil 66. Their hits included "The Look Of Love" (1968) and "The Fool On The Hill" (1968).
** EVENTS **
1573 : English explorer Francis Drake first saw the
Pacific Ocean.
1858 : 14 year-old BERNADETTE SOUBIROUS claimed to have
had visions of the Virgin Mary, near Lourdes in South-Western France. A spring of water at the grotto was reputed to have healing powers.
1861 : Explorers BURKE and WILLS reached the Gulf of
Carpentaria in Australia's North-East.
1914 : A French pilot flew over Mount Blanc in the Alps
to a height of 16,000 feet, from where he could see much of Europe.
1929 : Pope Pius XI and the Italian Government signed the
LATERAN TREATY, giving the Vatican City the status of an independent sovereign state.
1945 : WINSTON CHURCHILL, FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT and
JOSEPH STALIN met secretly in the Black Sea resort of Yalta, to map out the future of Europe, with victory in the war against Germany virtually assured.
1958 : Welsh psychoanalyst ERNEST JONES, disciple of
SIGMUND FREUD, died.
1962 : An Essex schoolboy claimed to have broken a world
record by dancing "The Twist" non-stop for 33 hours.
1973 : Australia's SHANE GOULD became the first woman to

swim 1500 metres in less than 17 minutes. At the national titles in Adelaide she took 3.7 seconds off her own world record with a time of 16 minutes, 56.9 seconds. She also holds the world records for the 100, 200 and 400 metres freestyle and 200 metres individual medley.
1975 : MARGARET THATCHER won the leadership of Britain's
Conservative Party, the first woman to take the post in the Party's 300-year history.
1983 : Briton DENNIS NILSEN was accused of killing
between 14 and 16 young men at his flat in North London.
1988 : Former UN Secretary-general KURT WALDHEIM

announced he planned to remain as President of Austria and ride out the storm over his second World War record. WALDHEIM, who was a German Army intelligence officer in the Balkans was accused of complicity in the deaths of thousands of Jews, Yugoslavs and Italians. A poll showed that 70 percent of Austrians thought he should not resign. He stayed but in 1991 announced he would not seek re-election.
1990 : African National Congress Leader NELSON MANDELA
was freed after spending 26 years in jail, for his opposition to the white South African Government's apartheid policies.
1990 : JAMES 'Buster' DOUGLAS won the world heavyweight
boxing title after knocking-out MIKE TYSON in Tokyo.
1991 : Soviet President MIKHAIL GORBACHEV notified Warsaw
Pact nations, proposing they disband the military structure from April 1. No text received
1994 : Five astronauts and a cosmonaut returned to Earth
aboard Discovery after the first joint U.S.-Russian space shuttle mission.
